key_insight: Evolving molten-zone geometry changes local solidification velocity, helping explain composition segregation beyond ideal Scheil–Pfann behaviour in Ni–Mn–Ga crystals.
engineering_relevance: Sapphire-confined optical floating-zone growth improves reproducibility and macroscopic geometry control, while modelling provides a basis for process optimisation.
method: Stabilise the molten zone inside a transparent sapphire crucible.
Couple transient COMSOL finite-element heat transfer to an effective molten-zone mass balance.
Reconstruct solidification conditions and longitudinal composition profiles.
evidence_signal: EBSD of a quenched interface independently supports the calculated front geometry, and the coupled model reproduces dominant features of measured composition profiles.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative prediction errors, so model accuracy and transferability to other growth conditions remain uncertain.
paper_title: Finite-element reconstruction of molten-zone dynamics and chemical segregation in optical floating-zone grown Ni--Mn--Ga
